description: The predicted intent is closely related and semantically adjacent to the expected intent, causing the bi-encoder to place the query near an overlapping intent cluster.
The query describes multiple distinct customer problems simultaneously, causing dense embedding vector averaging to focus on the secondary issue.
Relevant historical cases exist in Top-10, but the single customer-turn problem text representation ranked a distractor case higher due to lack of lexical discrimination.
The customer framed a functional/hardware symptom around an iOS update event (e.g. 'since iOS 11 update'), falsely pulling general OS update cases.
The query uses non-English words, heavy colloquialisms/slang, emotional venting, or atypical vocabulary divergent from curated historical cases.
The expected intent has very few historical training cases in the index (<200 cases), creating sparse vector coverage for that support domain.
Unique edge-case failure where symptom description does not align with standard error clusters.
The query is too short or lacks specific diagnostic keywords (e.g. <=8 words or vague requests), placing its vector near generic dense centroids.
